subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: continuous batching expectations and token economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeai.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: pricing & batching (post-demo recap + next steps)

Hi Alex - thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Recap:
- Primary workload: interactive customer support augmentation (live agent assist + bot handoff).
- Traffic profile (high level): ~20M-50M tokens/month expected in initial pilot; steady-state target 75M+ tokens/month if pilot is successful.
- Request mix: ~60% short queries (<200 tokens), ~30% mid (200-800), ~10% long (>800).
- Peak concurrency: observed bursts up to ~220 concurrent in-app sessions during business hours; effective QPS for generation ~60-120 qps in peaks.

Pricing / unit economics we discussed:
- Acme target monthly budget band: $10k- $30k for the pilot phase.
- Target unit goal (internal): ~$300-400 per 1M tokens to make the unit economics work for their GTM motion.
- With continuous batching and KV/prefix caching, we estimate 20%-40% effective token-cost reduction vs naive per-request serving.

Batching / concurrency assumptions:
- For interactive workloads like theirs, continuous batching (small window, e.g. 20-100ms) is very effective because requests stream in regularly from many users.
- We expect an average batch size of ~8-24 tokens per request (amortized across prompt + completion) and batching windows tuned to keep p99 latency inside their target (<= 400ms for conversational responses).
- For long requests (10% of traffic), throughput optimization favors larger per-request kernels; we can route those to slightly different instance types or allow higher batching windows.

Action items / next steps:
1) We will send a simple pricing model (attached) with a couple of scenarios: conservative, expected, and upside (includes continuous batching / cache assumptions).
2) Alex: can you confirm 2 things by EOD Wednesday? (a) whether the pilot budget is closer to $10k or $30k / month, and (b) whether you can share a 48-hour sample of request logs (sanitized) so our performance team can run a quick batching & concurrency sim.
3) If we get logs, we'll run a quick sim and return a revised $/1M tokens estimate and suggested Dedicated configuration within 3 business days.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-model-v2.xlsx (xlsx), mutual-action-plan.docx (docx)

Thanks - happy to hop back on a quick 20-min call if that helps.

- Marissa

Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & batching (post-demo recap + next steps)

Thanks Marissa - great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Budget: pilot is likely to be at the high end (~$25k/month) if performance proves out, with the ability to expand. We can justify up to $40k/month for the first 90 days if latency/accuracy meet SLAs.

2) Logs: we can share a sanitized 72-hour slice (we prefer 72h to capture weekday/weekend behavior). I will have Samantha pull and sanitize tonight; she will share a link with you. Expect things like user_id hashes and request/response token counts, timestamps, and latency.

3) Latency targets: to be competitive for live agent assist we need p95 < 250ms and p99 < 500ms for short queries. If continuous batching adds ~20-40% cost savings but pushes p99 > 500ms we'll want smaller windows.

4) Token mix: the 60/30/10 split looks right. Average prompt + response tokens per request is about ~220 tokens today (median ~180).

Next: Samantha will share logs; once you run sims let's align on a proposed pilot configuration and SLA.

- Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, Acme AI
alex.johnson@acmeai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & batching (post-demo recap + next steps)

Appreciate the fast follow-up, Alex - great to hear the pilot budget range. A couple of notes on the sim and pricing scenarios so expectations are clear:

Quick sim approach (what we'll run once we have sanitized logs):
- Ingest token-level timestamps and request sizes to produce an arrival distribution.
- Run our continuous-batching simulator with multiple window sizes (20ms, 50ms, 100ms) and measure simulated p95/p99, average batch size, and per-token compute cost.
- Model caching effects (prefix/KV cache) for repeated context patterns and compute expected cache hit rate.

Preliminary pricing scenarios (attached model includes detailed line items):
- Conservative: assumes limited batching (10% benefit) & low cache hit => estimate $420 / 1M tokens
- Expected: assumes steady continuous batching (25% benefit) & modest cache hit => estimate $310 / 1M tokens
- Upside: strong batching (35%+) & high cache hit from repeated prompts => estimate $230 / 1M tokens

Notes on how we calculate the $/1M tokens: combines GPU amortized cost, queueing overhead, model variant (quantized vs fp16), and cloud egress where applicable. We'll show the line items in the spreadsheet.

Suggested pilot config for target p95/p99 you gave:
- Dedicated small pool of 2 GPU instances (N1 sized) with burst capacity for peaks; autoscale policy: add one instance at sustained 60% utilization for >5m.
- Batching window default 50ms; reduce to 20ms if p99 creeps >500ms in sim.

Next steps:
1) Samantha: please share the sanitized 72h logs (link to Drive or S3).
2) We'll run the sim and post results + a recommended config + revised pricing table within 72 hours of ingest.
3) If results look good, propose we run a 30-day pilot with a capped spend of $25k and weekly check-ins.

If you're open I'm happy to book a 30-min sync after we share the sim results to walk the M A P and any technical tradeoffs.

- Marissa
